title: A Yearbook for the Prom
premise: August Sandoval, an eighteen-year-old coder, runs an anonymous account that exposes his school's darkest secrets—until he finds coded directions hidden in his late grandmother's recipe box revealing she ran the same account decades ago, and that she left one final post unsent. Following her trail, August discovers the account's original purpose wasn't cruelty but protection, and that the person his grandmother shielded is someone still at his school: his best friend Priya's grandmother, whose secret could unravel both families. As prom approaches, August must choose between posting the truth anonymously as he always has, or signing his name and risking the friendship that matters most. He ends by publishing the final post under both his and his grandmother's names, confessing everything to Priya at prom, and learning that being known is worth the cost of being seen.
about_author: Silas Fairweather is a former high school journalism teacher who spent a decade watching students trade truth for safety. He writes from a small coastal town where everyone's grandmother, he suspects, is keeping a recipe box of secrets.

chapters.title: The Careful Boy
chapters.summary: August's POV. We meet August three days before spring break: a meticulous coder whose anonymous account, 'The Yearbook,' knows every secret at Meridian High. He posts about a teacher's scandal, then scrubs his digital tracks with ritual precision. The emotional beat is controlled loneliness—he protects everyone by touching no one.

chapters.title: Grandma Rosa's Kitchen
chapters.summary: August's POV. Sorting his late grandmother's belongings with his mother, August finds her recipe box. Among the cardamom bread and mole recipes is a card with no food on it—just coordinates, dates, and a phrase he recognizes: the exact posting schedule of The Yearbook. Beat: vertigo disguised as grief.

chapters.title: Instructions Not for Eating
chapters.summary: August's POV, night scene. He decodes the card at his desk: his grandmother ran The Yearbook in 1974. The final card is sealed, marked 'unsent.' His hands shake as he realizes the account he thought he invented was inherited. Beat: the uncanny thrill of being seen by the dead.

chapters.title: Priya at the Window
chapters.summary: August's POV. Best friend Priya Rao climbs through his window like she has since freshman year, complaining about prom committee drama. August almost tells her everything, then deflects. A tender scene establishing their intimacy and the wall inside it. Beat: the ache of a half-kept secret.

chapters.title: The 1974 Archive
chapters.summary: August's POV. Digging through microfilm at the county library, August finds the original Yearbook posts—anonymous notes that exposed a wrongful expulsion in 1974 and saved a student named Kamala Rao. Priya's grandmother. Beat: the account was never cruelty; it was rescue.

chapters.title: What Grandma Buried
chapters.summary: August's POV, with a flashback to Rosa's 1974 diary entries. Rosa loved someone she couldn't name, and The Yearbook was her shield and her sword. The unsent final card, August realizes, is addressed to Kamala Rao—still alive, still two streets away. Beat: inheritance as unfinished business.

chapters.title: The New Post
chapters.summary: August's POV. Someone else posts to The Yearbook—something August didn't write—outing a closeted student. His account, his sanctuary, has been breached. Panic and fury. Beat: the protector's tools turned into a weapon.

chapters.title: Suspicions
chapters.summary: Priya's POV, first time. Priya notices August unraveling and starts her own quiet investigation, half-worried he's the anonymous poster everyone suddenly fears. Her loyalty wars with her suspicion. Beat: love learning to look closely.

chapters.title: Kamala Rao Answers the Door
chapters.summary: August's POV. He visits Kamala under a pretense, sees the sealed card's name on her mail, and flees without delivering it. Kamala watches him go with an expression that says she knows exactly who he is. Beat: cowardice with a witness.

chapters.title: The Breach Deepens
chapters.summary: August's POV, technical thriller chapter. August traces the impostor through server logs and finds the account was compromised through a shared password—one he gave to exactly one person, years ago, as a promise. Beat: betrayal as an arithmetic problem.

chapters.title: Prom Committee
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Prom planning collides with the scandal: the outed student's parents demand the dance be canceled, the school hunts the anonymous poster, and Priya defends The Yearbook's original purpose without knowing August's connection. Beat: public stakes for private truths.

chapters.title: The Person I Gave It To
chapters.summary: August's POV. He confronts the friend who leaked the password: Marcus, who used it not from malice but desperation—to out the boy who'd been cruel to his little brother. August must decide whether Marcus is a traitor or a mirror. Beat: rage softening into recognition.

chapters.title: Rosa's Unsent Card
chapters.summary: August's POV, quiet interlude. He finally opens the sealed card. Rosa's words to Kamala are not a confession of love but an apology for staying silent too long, and an instruction: 'Tell the truth while it can still be received kindly.' Beat: a grandmother's voice across fifty years.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: August's POV. A charged, almost-romantic evening with Priya—dinner, old songs, hands nearly touching. He comes within a sentence of telling her everything, including that her grandmother is the heart of the story. He doesn't. Beat: the cost of care, compounding interest.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The impostor posts again, this time threatening to reveal The Yearbook's original author's identity. Priya finds a 1974 photo in her grandmother's attic: Rosa and Kamala, holding hands, and a copy of the same recipe card. Beat: two investigations converging on one kitchen.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Diner
chapters.summary: August's POV. August and Priya, both armed with half the truth, meet accidentally at the diner where Rosa and Kamala used to sit. Accusations spill; Priya realizes August is The Yearbook. The friendship cracks open. Beat: the truth arriving too late and exactly on time.

chapters.title: What August Owes
chapters.summary: August's POV. Devastated, August visits Kamala and finally delivers Rosa's card. Kamala reads it, weeps, and tells him the story Rosa could never tell: they loved each other, and silence was the price of safety. She forgives Rosa; she asks August not to repeat her silence. Beat: absolution with conditions.

chapters.title: The Impostor's Last Post
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The impostor schedules a prom-night post that will out Rosa's story to the whole school, twisting it into scandal. Priya and August, barely speaking, independently discover the draft and realize they must work together to stop it—or answer it. Beat: enemies of the same lie.

chapters.title: All-Nighter
chapters.summary: August and Priya, alternating POV fragments. In his room, they rebuild the account together: Priya writes, August codes, and they draft a response post that tells the whole truth—Rosa and Kamala's story, August's inheritance, Marcus's pain—signed with real names. Beat: collaboration as reconciliation.

chapters.title: Prom
chapters.summary: August's POV. The gym in gold and navy, the impostor's post goes live, and chaos blooms. August walks to the middle of the dance floor, takes the microphone, and reads Rosa's card aloud before the crowd can finish consuming the scandal. Beat: the careful boy, finally loud.

chapters.title: The Final Post
chapters.summary: August's POV. That night, August publishes the last entry of The Yearbook—co-signed 'A. Sandoval & R. Sandoval, 1974–2025'—and then archives the account forever. Kamala reads it on her porch; Priya reads it in his window. Beat: inheritance completed, the weapon retired.

chapters.title: After the Dance
chapters.summary: August and Priya, shared POV. Graduation morning: Marcus forgiven, the outed student embraced by his class, Kamala and August planting Rosa's cardamom bread recipe in a new box. Priya takes his hand in daylight, in front of everyone. Beat: love against duty, duty finally yielding.
